method: CourtListener opinion text. No statutory publisher was reachable; every publisher, agency and mirror host returns 403 from this environment's egress policy, re-measured the same day.
queries: "Business and Professions Code section 16600" restraint of trade void employment

assertions.text: non-compete provisions are void under California law
assertions.note: Section 16600 quoted verbatim by the California Supreme Court in Ixchel.

assertions.text: it is unlawful to include or attempt to enforce them
assertions.note: This is a different and stronger claim than voidness — it asserts the act of including the term is itself unlawful. A targeted search returned no opinion construing the provision the clause relies on for it; the single hit predates the 2023 legislation entirely and is a false match. Absence of evidence, not evidence of error — but the clause states it as settled and nothing in this channel supports it.

assertions.text: regardless of where the agreement is signed or which state's law it names
assertions.note: Extraterritorial reach is a separate provision from the one the clause cites. Neither the cited section nor the cited session law was shown to carry it, and no opinion construing it was located. The clause's own citation does not reach its own claim.

assertions.text: customer non-solicitation covenants are void on the same basis
assertions.note: The clause merges customer non-solicits and non-competes into one rule. The decisions located analyse employee non-solicits and general restraints; none was found holding customer non-solicits void as a category. Needs its own check before this sentence is relied on.

gaps: The statute begins 'Except as provided in this chapter,' and the Supreme Court in Ixchel traced those exceptions to restraints on the sale of goodwill and on dissolution of a partnership. This clause sits in a template used by companies whose founders hold equity they may later sell. It states the rule with no indication that any exception exists.

Ixchel held the section does not apply per se to contracts between businesses, which get a rule-of-reason analysis instead. The clause states the rule flatly; a reader applying it to a vendor or channel agreement would be applying the wrong standard.

sources.title: CourtListener — Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc. (Cal. 2020), quoting Bus. & Prof. Code §16600

judicialQuotations.case: Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc. (Cal. 2020)
judicialQuotations.quote: Except as provided in this chapter, every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void.

judicialQuotations.case: Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc. (Cal. 2020)
judicialQuotations.quote: As noted, the Legislature in 1872 adopted Civil Code former section 1673, which provided: "Every contract by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind, otherwise than is provided by the next two sections, is to that extent void." The next two sections excepted certain contractual restraints upon the sale of goodwill in a business (Civ. Code, former § 1674) or upon dissolution of a partnership (Civ. Code, former § 1675).

singleOpinionCaveat: One California Supreme Court opinion quoting the statute. Strong for the text, but still one court's transcription of a statute this environment cannot reach directly. It does not meet the two-primary standard and upgrades nothing.
